issue_context.title: Zone boundaries innacurate since 2024.2
issue_context.body:
### The problem

Since 2024.2 zone boundaries are no longer accurate.  A user can be well outside the boundary but HA still shows the user inside it.

![Untitled picture](https://github.com/home-assistant/core/assets/1779529/e35a9ae6-bcfa-41ea-b2d9-b68dd6b7c87a)

This user is showing in HA as inside the zone.  The user will only show as outside the zone once they are over 3 miles from the zone boundary.  The previous version of HA (2024.1) would show the user as outside the zone as soon as they cross the boundary.

For testing purposes I rolled back to 2024.1 and I can verify that this new behaviour wasn't present in that version.


### What version of Home Assistant Core has the issue?

core-2024.2.0

### What was the last working version of Home Assistant Core?

core-2024.1

### What type of installation are you running?

Home Assistant OS

### Integration causing the issue

Zone

https://www.home-assistant.io/integrations/zone/

I've been experiencing this as well since upgrading to 2024.2 (although the distance doesn't seem to be as drastic as yours).

I started noticing that my arrival automation was triggering roughly 15-20 seconds earlier than it used to on 2024.1 and below. Looking at the logs, my device tracker entity switches to `home` about 500ft outside the zone (the default `zone.home`) and the zone itself also increments its state as well.

In contrast, the companion app doesn't send a `GEOFENCE_ENTER` event until I actually enter the zone (as defined by my coords & the default 100m radius). I also see a regular `FLP_BACKGROUND` event with the same timestamp time as the device tracker entity update in the server logs. This event's coordinates and accuracy are correct on the map, so it doesn't appear to be an incorrect GPS reading; rather it looks like the server is now miscalculating the zone arrival (in contrast to the companion app which sends the zone entry event at the correct distance).

In addition to seeing this about 8-10 times in the real world over the past few days, I can also reproduce it 100% reliably using GPS spoofing on my phone. I move my location outside the zone (but within that roughly 500ft distance that it seems to be miscalculating) and the phone sends a `GEOFENCE_EXIT` event, but my device tracker entity remains set to `home` and `zone.home` does not decrement. Once I move the fake location sufficiently further away, a regular `FLP_BACKGROUND` event coincides with my device tracker update to `not_home` and `zone.home` decrementing by one. I notice the same behavior conversely; once `not_home`, I move the location back within that error boundary of ~ 500ft and see the arrival automations running early (device tracker switch to `home` and `zone.home` increment). Again, once I move my fake location back within the **true** `zone.home` radius, I see the companion app send the `GEOFENCE_ENTER` event, but the server already thinks I'm home.

The zone integration had some changes for 2024.2 release, could that be the cause?

https://github.com/home-assistant/core/pull/108629/commits/91f0c28a19d2f43f378fd4374f8230a94c46e180

I saw that, and was actually in the process of manually editing the zone/\_\_init\_\_.py file in my docker instance (on latest 2024.2) to see if that fixes it. Will report back later today on my findings.

I just confirmed that reverting that single commit (PR #108629) fixes the issue for me - at least using spoofed GPS. I'm going to keep the code reverted and will also verify using real GPS data later in the day. 

@bdraco, it looks like that zone clean-up PR introduced a regression which is causing trackers to appear within a zone when they are actually outside it. Please let me know if you need any more debugging info and I can gladly assist.
Just to follow up - confirmed the revert has worked well in real world scenarios about 4 times yesterday.
Oh I see the bug. The radius var is shadowed.

Just updated my local instance with the `__init__.py` file from #110354 and it corrects the issue (with GPS spoofing) for me. I can update later once I head out for an errand, but am fairly confident that everything is good with the update. Thanks!
Thanks. I tagged the fix for 2024.2.2
